segments.title: Opening, Houston setting, the unfinished book and photos
segments.summary: Allen opens the tape; Bauduc talks about his book with a newspaper writer and shows photos including the Swing That Music pictures.

segments.title: Family names, father Jules Sr., and the Henry Raymond relation
segments.summary: Bauduc explains his family and names, and a distant relation to clarinetist Henry Raymond. He recalls Milneburg picnics with bands.

segments.title: The Cajun country story and the left-hand drum pedal
segments.summary: He retells his story of a gig with beaten-up instruments and a left-hand-thread pedal, fixed on the spot.

segments.title: Father's playing, brother Jules, and walking away from reading music
segments.summary: His father played in the French Opera House and the union; Bauduc learned drums at home, tried Kid Peterson's lessons and chose to play his own way.

segments.title: Hearing music at home and the Mares family band
segments.summary: As a child he heard family music; Paul Mares's father practised nearby with his father.

segments.title: Why he never learned to read and his melodic drum style
segments.summary: He declined studio reading work, and describes his accented triplets and melodic approach versus modern drummers.

segments.title: Bulls on Parade and the marching clubs
segments.summary: He recalls a Black parade organization with a bull on ropes, the origin of his parade tune for Bob Crosby.

segments.title: French at home and leaving St. Aloysius College
segments.summary: His parents spoke French; he was placed in a French class, was laughed at, tore up the book and left school.

segments.title: Delgado Trade School, Emmett Hardy and Bill Eastwood
segments.summary: At Delgado he jammed at lunch with Emmett Hardy and Eastwood and played jobs with them.

segments.chapter: Johnny Bayersdorffer band and early drummers
segments.title: Leaving with Johnny Bayersdorffer and the Tokyo Gardens
segments.summary: He joined Bayersdorffer to see the world, played two seasons at Tokyo Gardens, and band members came and went.

segments.chapter: Johnny Bayersdorffer band and early drummers
segments.title: Robichaud's band, Tranchina's and Up a Lazy River
segments.summary: They discuss the left-handed fiddler Robichaud and who wrote Up a Lazy River.

segments.chapter: Johnny Bayersdorffer band and early drummers
segments.title: Meeting Hoagy Carmichael in Indiana
segments.summary: Bauduc met Hoagy at Indiana University and played parties for him; he played by ear.

segments.chapter: Johnny Bayersdorffer band and early drummers
segments.title: Comparing Robichaud and Piron
segments.summary: Allen and Bauduc sort out which bandleader was the left-handed fiddler.

segments.chapter: Johnny Bayersdorffer band and early drummers
segments.title: Zutty Singleton, the borrowed cymbal and the two drummers called Happy
segments.summary: He tells of Zutty at the Lyric, a Zildjian cymbal, their friendship, and which Happy drummer was meant.

segments.chapter: Johnny Bayersdorffer band and early drummers
segments.title: Forming the Six Nola Jazz and the Dixieland Rompers
segments.summary: He recalls his first band, its members, and the name change to Dixieland Rompers, first to broadcast live.

segments.title: The radio broadcast from the De Soto hotel
segments.summary: They recall the live radio show location and singer Eddie McCarty.

segments.title: Band photographs, his father's park band and a forgotten singer
segments.summary: Looking at pictures: the Rompers, his father in Joe Spora's band, and a blonde singer with Bob Crosby whose name escapes them.

segments.title: The photo backstage at the Apollo with Louis Armstrong
segments.summary: He tells how a photographer took a picture as they visited Armstrong backstage in New York.

segments.title: His drum kit, cowbells and the singer's name again
segments.summary: They discuss his Ludwig set and four cowbells, then return to the missing singer's name.

segments.title: Paul DeDroit as a drummer and Leonard Bayersdorffer's piano
segments.summary: He assesses Paul DeDroit and brother Johnny, their sitting in, and the piano tuned a half tone high.

segments.title: Mardi Gras clubs, Indians and the Irish Channel
segments.summary: Allen asks about marching clubs; Bauduc recalls Black Indian parades and playing church dances.

segments.title: First job with Paul DeDroit on Mardi Gras day
segments.summary: He recalls carrying his bass drum across Canal Street to a Mardi Gras job with Paul DeDroit.

segments.chapter: Reading, repertoire and New Orleans players
segments.title: Leo Addy and New Orleans drummers who did not read
segments.summary: Allen asks about Leo Addy; Bauduc says New Orleans players mostly played by ear and avoided corny Dixieland.

segments.chapter: Reading, repertoire and New Orleans players
segments.title: Credit due to the New Orleans Rhythm Kings and Rappolo
segments.summary: He argues the Rhythm Kings deserve more credit and describes Rappolo's clarinet style.

segments.chapter: Reading, repertoire and New Orleans players
segments.title: Tunes of the early bands and his parade tune
segments.summary: He discusses Diane, the blues, Fidgety Feet and Panama, and building those ideas into his parade tune.

segments.chapter: Reading, repertoire and New Orleans players
segments.title: Baby Dodds and reading versus playing your own way
segments.summary: He speaks of Baby Dodds and says great players like Bix played their own way.

segments.chapter: Reading, repertoire and New Orleans players
segments.title: Kid Rena's drummer and Kid Punch
segments.summary: They recall Chani and Kid Punch, and clubs such as the Pelican and Sam Morgan's.

segments.chapter: Reading, repertoire and New Orleans players
segments.title: Monk Hazel and brother Jules's band
segments.summary: He recalls Monk Hazel in his brother's band and later with Sharkey.

segments.chapter: Reading, repertoire and New Orleans players
segments.title: Blues singers: Udell Wilson and Willie Jackson
segments.summary: Asked about blues, he recalls pianist Udell Wilson and singer Willie Jackson, and says he plays his own way.

segments.title: Pinky Vodakovich, Bill Padron and playing waltzes
segments.summary: They name New Orleans musicians, then he says he played waltzes at Tokyo Gardens and with Crosby.

segments.title: Bayersdorffer band personnel: Loicano, Webber, Bouchon and Krieger
segments.summary: He recalls who joined and left Johnny's band, including Loicano, Webber, Bouchon, Lefty and Krieger.
